question: An increase in blood pressure between 80 and 150 mmHg increases diuresis because:

options.opb: Decreases the peritubular reabsorption of water.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Increase in blood pressure" -> "Increased glomerular filtration rate" -> "Increased urine production" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Increase in blood pressure" -> "Increased renal blood flow" -> "Increased glomerular filtration" -> "Increased diuresis" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Increase in blood pressure" -> "Decreased peritubular reabsorption of water" -> "Increased urine output" -> 75%
CHAIN: "Increase in blood pressure" -> "Efferent arteriole contraction" -> "Increased glomerular pressure" -> "Increased filtration" -> "Increased diuresis" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Increase in blood pressure" -> "Afferent arteriole contraction" -> "Possible decrease in glomerular filtration" -> "Unclear effect on diuresis" -> 50%
analysis: An increase in blood pressure within the range of 80 to 150 mmHg enhances renal perfusion and glomerular filtration rate (GFR), leading to increased diuresis. This is primarily due to the proportional increase in renal blood flow, which facilitates greater filtration of plasma and subsequently more urine production.
